chunks: Isma'il al-Ju'fi said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام:
A man loves Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, but he does not dissociate himself from his enemy, and he says: He is dearer to me than those who opposed him.
He said: This one is mixed, and he is an enemy; so do not perform salat (prayer) behind him, and there is no honor for him, except that you fear him as a precaution.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام
key_terms.تَتَّقِيَهُ: guard yourself from him; act out of precautionary fear
key_terms.تُصَلِّ وَرَاءَهُ: perform salat (prayer) behind him as an Imam in congregation
key_terms.عَدُوٌّ: enemy; one treated as hostile in religious allegiance
key_terms.عَدُوِّهِ: his enemy; the enemy of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام
key_terms.مِخْلَطٌ: mixed; a person of confused or compromised belief

ai.seo_question: Can one pray behind a person who claims love for Imam Ali عليه السلام but does not disassociate from his enemies?
ai.summary: This hadith states that merely claiming love for Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام is not sufficient if one does not also disavow his enemies. It further gives a legal ruling that such a person should not be followed in congregational salat (prayer), except in a case of precautionary fear.
